title: Kitchen-table hiring reflection — Marco Rios
content:
Context: late-night brain dump after loop for Senior Runtime Engineer. Not polished — my private passback for hiring committee and a quick draft of a scorecard to iterate on.

Role fit synopsis (30s): strong systems instincts, good latency-oriented mental model, solid tradeoffs on caching vs memory. Not sure about team-level mentorship/initiative fit yet (needs evidence).

What I liked (concrete):
- Recreated the KV cache eviction sketch on the whiteboard with edge-case reasoning (TTL vs size-based evict). Showed they think about skyline and across-tenant fairness.
- Clear cost-latency tradeoff examples: emphasized prioritizing tail latency for web-facing routes, acceptable to move throughput-heavy batch jobs to background workers.
- Gave a neat analogy for dynamic batching: "like pulse-scheduling on an airport runway" — explained backpressure well.

Concerns / red flags (prioritized):
1) Perf microbenching literacy: when I asked about how they'd instrument a regression, initial answer leaned purely on flamegraphs and p95 logging; missed KV cache hit-rate sampling and sequence-length stratification. Could be a gap or just short explanation under pressure.
2) Sketchy infra ops history: their dedicated infra experience is limited — mostly multi-tenant hosted infra. For Dedicated offering we need someone who can own infra upgrades and node-level debugging.
3) Ambiguous on cross-team communication: examples were individual contributor-heavy; didn't surface examples of leading rollouts or owning an incident comms channel.

Coding exercise recollection: implemented a simplified concurrent LRU in the pairing session. Code worked but used coarse-grained locks; when I pushed for contention-free approaches they mentioned sharding but couldn't quickly sketch a lock-free design. That may be fine for many workloads, but worth noting for high-throughput inference paths.

Behavioral / culture signals:
- Curious, asks clarifying questions early — good sign.
- Calm under pressure, gave concise answers when interrupted.
- Slightly transactional framing around career goals (wants to move quickly into IC impact), unclear appetite for manager-track coaching.

Suggested scorecard bullets (raw draft):
- Systems design (0–5): 4 — thoughtful about latency and tradeoffs, strong intuition.
- Performance debugging (0–5): 3 — practical, misses a couple observability levers we use.
- Concurrency & correctness (0–5): 3 — correct but coarse-grained implementations; can mature to 4 with pairing.
- Ownership & cross-team (0–5): 2.5 — needs stronger signals on shipping cross-functional projects.
- Communication (0–5): 4 — clear verbal explanations, good clarifying questions.
- Overall recommendation: weak hire / hire with conditions (pairing trial + small ownership project).

Concrete next-steps I propose (order matters):
1) Short 1-week pairing eval on a small runtime perf bug with one of us as mentor (2–3 sessions). Evaluate how they handle code ownership, test strategy, and perf validation.
2) Ask for a written 1-pager within 48h: a simple plan to diagnose a hypothetical 30% p99 increase on text-generation endpoints (what metrics, what experiments, rollback plan). This tests observability thinking in writing.
3) If both pass, offer with an explicit 6-month ramp goal: lead a small rollout (canary + metrics gating) for an optimization (batching or kv-cache).

Open questions / things to verify in reference checks:
- Which specific perf regressions did they own and what was the observable impact? (numbers help).
- Did they ever run canary rollouts end-to-end (metrics gating, rollback thresholds)?
- Examples of mentoring/knowledge transfer (docs, runbooks, postmortems).

Quick note to hiring manager: this candidate will move the needle on latency-focused tasks quickly but needs scaffolding for ops/ownership. If we hire, set up a first 30/60/90 plan with an explicit canary project and pairing mentor.

Random scratch ideas to include in official feedback (clean later):
- Mention the airport runway analogy — makes the candidate memorable.
- Call out the KV eviction sketch as a specific example of systems thoughtfulness.
- Prefer conditional offer language: "hire pending pairing trial and written perf-plan".

Unresolved / my own doubts:
- Was the limited ops experience a true gap or a pressure artefact? Pairing trial should resolve.
- Could be a mid-level IC disguised as senior due to strong surface-level vocabulary. Verify with references and the written plan.

Time-stamped scribbles:
- 21:05 — pairing started, implemented LRU in ~25 mins.
- 21:35 — asked about instrumentation, leaned on flamegraphs; follow-up asked about sampling by sequence length, prodded on histograms, candidate pivoted.
- 21:55 — moderation: thoughtful but a few gaps.

Send to: hiring loop thread + attach to LIN-4821. Draft a tidied scorecard after feedback from Avery.

End of scratch — will clean and push to shared hiring doc if we decide to move forward.
